items.stem: Which of the following best describes "CO₂-equivalent (CO₂e)"?
options: A measure of how much heat a greenhouse gas traps over a period (usually 100 years) relative to the same mass of CO₂
Greenhouse-gas emissions caused by human activities such as burning fossil fuels, deforestation, agriculture and industry
A process that amplifies (positive) or dampens (negative) an initial change in climate
The amount of CO₂ that would have the same warming effect as a given mass of another greenhouse gas, calculated as mass × GWP
items.answer: The amount of CO₂ that would have the same warming effect as a given mass of another greenhouse gas, calculated as mass × GWP
items.markingKey: D. "CO₂-equivalent (CO₂e)" is the amount of CO₂ that would have the same warming effect as a given mass of another greenhouse gas, calculated as mass × GWP.

items.stem: Explain why per-capita emissions are important when comparing countries.
items.answer: Total emissions reflect population size; per-capita figures show the lifestyle and energy intensity of residents and are central to debates about fairness (e.g. USA ~15 t vs India ~2 t CO₂ per person).
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Total emissions reflect population size; per-capita figures show the lifestyle and energy intensity of residents and are central to debates about fairness (e.g. USA ~15 t vs India ~2 t CO₂ per person). items.markingKey: Global warming is caused by greenhouse gases trapping infrared radiation; the ozone hole lets in more UV but has little effect on global temperature. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Explain why methane is an important target for climate policy despite its lower concentration than CO₂.
items.answer: Per molecule it traps much more heat (GWP₁₀₀ ≈ 28, GWP₂₀ ≈ 80), and its short lifetime (~12 years) means cuts quickly reduce warming; it is responsible for about 30% of warming since pre-industrial times.

items.stem: Annual mean CO₂ at Mauna Loa (ppm): 1960: 316.9; 1970: 325.7; 1980: 338.8; 1990: 354.4; 2000: 369.7; 2010: 389.9; 2015: 401.0; 2020: 414.2; 2023: 421.1. (a) Calculate the mean rate of increase for 1960-1990 and for 1990-2020 and comment on the trend. (b) Using the 2015-2023 rate, estimate the year in which 450 ppm will be reached. (c) Explain the small seasonal cycle superimposed on this trend.
items.answer: (a) 1.25 ppm/yr and 1.99 ppm/yr - the rate of increase is accelerating as emissions grew (b) rate = (421.1 − 401.0)/8 = 2.51 ppm/yr; (450 − 421.1)/rate ≈ 12 years → about 2035 (c) Northern Hemisphere vegetation draws down CO₂ by photosynthesis in summer and releases it by respiration/decomposition in winter.
items.markingKey: (a) A1 1.25, A1 1.99, R1 acceleration. (b) A1 ≈ 2035. (c) R1 seasonal photosynthesis vs respiration.

items.stem: Outline the meaning of the term "enhanced greenhouse effect".
items.answer: The increase in the natural greenhouse effect caused by human emissions of greenhouse gases, leading to global warming

items.stem: Which tipping element could raise sea level by several metres over centuries if it collapsed?
items.answer: The West Antarctic Ice Sheet
items.markingKey: D. It holds enough ice for about 3-5 m of sea-level rise.

items.stem: The IPCC Sixth Assessment Report (2021) concluded that human influence on warming is:
items.answer: "unequivocal"
items.markingKey: B. Earlier reports used "very likely" (2007) and "extremely likely" (2013).

items.stem: A student claims: "Sea-level rise is caused only by melting sea ice." Identify the error in this claim and correct it.
items.answer: Melting floating sea ice does not raise sea level significantly; thermal expansion and melting land ice (glaciers, Greenland and Antarctic ice sheets) cause the rise.
items.markingKey: Melting floating sea ice does not raise sea level significantly; thermal expansion and melting land ice (glaciers, Greenland and Antarctic ice sheets) cause the rise. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Explain the difference between per-capita emissions and total national emissions.
items.answer: Total emissions measure a country's overall contribution (China is largest); per-capita emissions divide by population, showing that people in some smaller countries (Qatar, Australia, USA) emit much more each.
items.markingKey: Total emissions measure a country's overall contribution (China is largest); per-capita emissions divide by population, showing that people in some smaller countries (Qatar, Australia, USA) emit much more each. items.stem: Explain how clouds can act as both positive and negative feedbacks.
items.answer: More low, thick clouds reflect sunlight (cooling - negative); more high, thin cirrus trap long-wave radiation (warming - positive); the overall effect is likely slightly positive but is the largest source of uncertainty.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: More low, thick clouds reflect sunlight (cooling - negative); more high, thin cirrus trap long-wave radiation (warming - positive); the overall effect is likely slightly positive but is the largest source of uncertainty. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Explain the difference between instrumental data and proxy data.
items.answer: Proxy data (ice cores, tree rings, corals) indirectly record past climate over thousands of years but with greater uncertainty; instrumental data are direct measurements (thermometers, satellites) available only for about the last 170 years.
items.markingKey: Proxy data (ice cores, tree rings, corals) indirectly record past climate over thousands of years but with greater uncertainty; instrumental data are direct measurements (thermometers, satellites) available only for about the last 170 years. items.stem: State two differences between impacts on ecosystems and impacts on societies.
items.answer: Ecosystem impacts include range shifts, bleaching, phenological mismatch and extinction risk; societal impacts include crop losses, water shortages, flooding of settlements, health effects and migration - the two are linked because societies depend on ecosystem services.
items.markingKey: Ecosystem impacts include range shifts, bleaching, phenological mismatch and extinction risk; societal impacts include crop losses, water shortages, flooding of settlements, health effects and migration - the two are linked because societies depend on ecosystem services. items.stem: Explain how burning fossil fuels enhances the greenhouse effect.
items.answer: Combustion transfers carbon stored for millions of years into the atmosphere as CO₂; higher concentrations absorb more outgoing long-wave radiation, reducing heat loss to space and raising the equilibrium temperature.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: Combustion transfers carbon stored for millions of years into the atmosphere as CO₂; higher concentrations absorb more outgoing long-wave radiation, reducing heat loss to space and raising the equilibrium temperature. items.stem: Outline three lines of evidence that the climate is warming.
items.answer: Rising global surface temperatures (~1.1-1.3 °C); sea-level rise (~20 cm since 1900, accelerating); shrinking Arctic sea ice and glaciers; ocean heat content increasing; earlier springs and shifting species ranges.

items.stem:
Refer to the data below.

Projected global mean sea-level rise by 2100 relative to 1995-2014 (IPCC AR6, likely range): SSP1-2.6 (low emissions) 0.32-0.62 m; SSP2-4.5 0.44-0.76 m; SSP5-8.5 (very high emissions) 0.63-1.01 m.

Explain why sea level will continue to rise after 2100 even under low emissions.
items.answer: Oceans continue to warm and expand for centuries (thermal inertia), and ice sheets respond slowly to past warming.

items.answer: (a) 2,700 + 133 × 28 + 9 × 265 = 8,809 t CO₂e (b) methane 42%; largest: CH₄ (c) methane has a short lifetime (~12 years) but is very potent, so over 20 years its warming effect is about 80 times CO₂; cutting methane (leaks, landfill, livestock) gives rapid near-term cooling, as targeted by the Global Methane Pledge (30% by 2030).
